channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: PL já alinhou discurso sobre ausência de mulher na chapa de Flávio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign has prepared talking points to counter criticism over the absence of a woman on their 'pure-blood' presidential ticket, after months of stating he wanted a woman as his running mate. Despite this, he announced today that deputy Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL) will be his vice-presidential candidate, keeping the ticket all-male. The strategy aims to minimize the impact of lacking female representation in the 2026 race.

item.title: Lula e Alcolumbre se reúnem em jantar com ministros do STF
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Congress President Davi Alcolumbre met for a dinner after months of no contact, signaling a political reconciliation effort. The meeting was facilitated by Supreme Court Justices Alexandre de Moraes and Cristiano Zanin, with other STF ministers also in attendance. The gathering reflects an attempt to ease institutional tensions and restore dialogue between the Executive and Legislative branches.

item.title: A indireta de Flávio a Alckmin, ao anunciar seu vice
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro criticized Geraldo Alckmin when announcing his running mate, Alfredo Gaspar, implying that Alckmin 'returns to the scene of the crime' by supporting Lula after previously accusing him of 'destroying Brazil' in 2017. The jab references Alckmin's past statement as a tucano, now reversed as he joins Lula's ticket.

item.title: Quem é Alfredo Gaspar, escolhido vice na chapa de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Federal Deputy Alfredo Gaspar has been chosen as the vice-presidential candidate on Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) ticket for the 2026 elections. Gaspar, who joined the PL in March 2024, is known for serving as rapporteur of the INSS CPI, which investigated fraud in the National Institute of Social Security. His nomination strengthens Bolsonaro's strategy of forming a pure-blood Bolsonarist ticket.

item.title: Ao escolher Alfredo Gaspar, Flávio aposta em combate à corrupção, não em economia, para a vice
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro selected Alfredo Gaspar as his running mate, prioritizing anti-corruption credentials over economic expertise. Gaspar, a former prosecutor and rapporteur of the INSS CPMI, gained national prominence for investigating pension fraud and financial crimes, but lacks experience in economic policy or congressional negotiations for structural reforms. The choice signals that the campaign believes anti-corruption rhetoric will mobilize more voters than selecting a vice president capable of reassuring financial markets.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro anuncia Alfredo Gaspar como seu vice na chapa à presidência
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro announced federal deputy Alfredo Gaspar (PL-BA) as his vice-presidential running mate for the 2026 presidential ticket. The announcement was made during a PL party meeting in Brasília, broadcast on the senator's social media, after weeks of uncertainty. The ticket is described as 'pure blood,' aligned with other right-wing candidates.

item.title: Alfredo Gaspar será o candidato a vice-presidente na chapa de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro has nominated Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL) as his vice-presidential running mate for the 2026 election, following failed attempts to form alliances with centrist parties. The decision reflects the PL's political isolation after Republicans, Brazil Union and Podemos declared neutrality. Gaspar, who served as rapporteur of the INSS scandal CPMI, was chosen over alternatives including a female candidate and Rogério Marinho, reinforcing the campaign's focus on linking Lula to corruption.

item.title: Marcola deixa a campanha do presidente Lula
item.description: Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro, known as Marcola, left the re-election campaign of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on Wednesday (August 5), following reports that he may have received payments from businesswoman and lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, who is allegedly a partner of Antônio Carlos Camilo Antunes, known as 'Careca do INSS'. Marcola had served as Lula's chief of staff after the president's third-term inauguration and had recently joined the campaign team. His departure comes amid growing concerns over potential conflicts of interest and irregularities in campaign financing.

item.title: Ao lado de 6 mulheres, Flávio anuncia Alfredo Gaspar como vice
item.description: Senator and presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) announced federal deputy Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL) as his running mate in an event alongside six women. The decision came after Republicans and Progressistas chose neutrality, ruling out names like Daniella Marques (Republicanos) and Tereza Cristina (PP-MS). The report will be updated.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro anuncia Alfredo Gaspar, relator da comissão do INSS, como vice
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL's presidential candidate, announced federal deputy Alfredo Gaspar (AL) as his running mate for the 2026 elections. Gaspar serves as rapporteur of the mixed CPI on INSS, focusing on pension reform and public resource management. The alliance strengthens the conservative and pro-pension stance of the Bolsonaro campaign.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro define Alfredo Gaspar como vice em chapa puro-sangue
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) announced federal deputy Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL) as his running mate in a pure-slate ticket for the 2026 presidential election. The announcement was made in Brasília on the final day of party conventions, ending weeks of speculation. Gaspar, a Northeasterner, stressed loyalty, fighting corruption and organized crime, while Valdemar Costa Neto confirmed the choice had been made six months prior.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro anuncia Alfredo Gaspar como vice na disputa à Presidência
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, senator from PL-RJ and presidential candidate, announced deputy Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL) as his running mate for the 2026 presidential election. The announcement was made in Brasília, with thanks to the women considered for the ticket, including Tereza Cristina, Daniella Marques, Damares Alves, Bia Kicis, Renata Abreu, Michelle Bolsonaro, and Julia Zanatta.

item.title: Relator da CPMI do INSS é escolhido vice de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Federal deputy Alfredo Gaspar (PL-RN) has been selected as the vice-presidential running mate for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) in the 2026 presidential election. Gaspar gained national prominence as the rapporteur of the INSS Parliamentary Inquiry Committee (CPMI), which investigated alleged irregularities in the social security agency's management. Prior to this, he was preparing to run for a Senate seat in Rio Grande do Norte.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro anuncia deputado Alfredo Gaspar como vice na chapa dele à Presidência
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro announced federal deputy Alfredo Gaspar as his vice-presidential candidate for the 2026 elections. Gaspar, a former prosecutor and rapporteur of the INSS CPI, was highlighted for his work in public security and defense of retirees. The announcement ends weeks of PL negotiations, after other parties chose to remain neutral in the presidential race.

item.title: Lula recebe assessor de Putin fora da agenda oficial
item.description: President Lula met with Nikolai Patrushev, Putin's advisor and head of Russia's Maritime Council, in an unofficial meeting to discuss bilateral cooperation and international security. Later that day, Lula called Putin to address the Ukraine war and bilateral trade, expressing disappointment with the UN Security Council's inability to resolve conflicts and emphasizing the need for dialogue among major powers. Patrushev also held meetings with Celso Amorim, Itamaraty's secretary-general, the Brazilian Navy commander, and officials from the Ministries of Ports and Airports and of Development, Industry, Commerce and Services, focusing on maritime, scientific, technological and defense collaboration.

item.title: Ex-chefe de gabinete decide deixar a campanha de Lula
item.description: Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro, known as Marcola, former chief of staff to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, decided to leave the coordination of Lula’s reelection campaign after it was revealed he took out a R$ 249,000 loan with businesswoman Roberta Luchsinger, a transaction under investigation by the Federal Police. Marcola had left his position at the Planalto in July to join the campaign team, resuming the role he held in 2022. His departure is attributed to the need to focus on his personal defense, amid allegations of internal opposition within the campaign.

item.title: Ex-chefe de gabinete de Lula pede para deixar a campanha do petista
item.description: Former chief of staff to Lula, Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro, known as Marcola, requested to leave the president's re-election campaign after revelations that he received payments from lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, who is under investigation by the Federal Police for alleged influence within the INSS under the PT administration. The move comes amid investigations into potential financial irregularities tied to the Lula government.

item.title: Mendonça cobra dados do governo Lula sobre gastos com publicidade para verificar se valores obedeceram teto
item.description: TSE Vice President André Mendonça has given the Lula government 10 days to provide data on advertising spending in the first half of 2026 to verify compliance with legal spending limits. The request partially grants a representation filed by the campaign of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), which alleges excessive institutional advertising. Mendonça emphasized the measure does not presuppose fraud and is intended solely to analyze the timing and nature of expenditures, without prejudging the final outcome.

item.title: Ex-chefe de gabinete de Lula pede para deixar campanha
item.description: Marco Aurélio Ribeiro, former chief of staff to President Lula and known as Marcola, decided to step down from Lula's campaign after reports emerged of a R$ 249,000 loan he took from lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, a friend of the president's son, Lulinha. Although he stated he has repaid the debt and reaffirmed his commitment to ethics and transparency, Marcola said his departure is a political decision to avoid becoming a target of internal PT disputes and friendly fire, thereby protecting Lula's campaign. The PT is trying to persuade him to stay, but sources say he is considered irreconcilable.

item.title: Mendonça Filho une direita em Pernambuco e vai disputar o Senado
item.description: Mendonça Filho (PL-PE) announced his candidacy for the Brazilian Senate from Pernambuco, uniting conservative right-wing supporters after being left without space in União Brasil. He received endorsements from Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), Anderson Ferreira (PL), and Gilson Machado (Pode), as well as the influential Coelho clan, and will be the sole slate for Flávio Bolsonaro in the state.

item.title: Lula e Alcolumbre se encontram na casa de Moraes após rompimento; senador fala em 'segredo'
item.description: Lula and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre met at the residence of Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes following months of estrangement, facilitated also by Justice Cristiano Zanin, to 'break the ice' and restore relations. The meeting, described as positive by aides, lasted two to three hours and focused on overcoming past grievances, with specific topics deferred until after the elections. Alcolumbre declined to elaborate, stating only that the discussion was a 'secret'.

item.title: Meio/Ideia: Lula preserva vantagem sobre Flávio Bolsonaro; concentração de votos nos dois cresce
item.description: Lula maintains an eight-point lead over Flávio Bolsonaro, with 43% and 35% voting intentions, respectively. The race is increasingly concentrated between the two, totaling 78% of the electorate, while alternative candidates remain weak. Despite their lead, both candidates exhibit high rejection rates, signaling a polarized electorate.

item.title: Brasil decide adotar reciprocidade contra os EUA após revogação do visto de embaixadora
item.description: The Lula government has decided to apply diplomatic reciprocity against the United States following the revocation of the visa of Brazil's ambassador to Washington, Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti, which Brasília views as a deliberate escalation of hostile measures. The U.S. action is reportedly a reaction to Brazil's refusal to grant diplomatic approval for Daniel Perez to assume the U.S. ambassadorship in Brasília, a move Brazil claims violates the confidentiality of the agrément process under the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations.

item.title: Para 59%, manifestação de paz entre Michelle e Flávio Bolsonaro foi positiva, diz Genial/Quaest
item.description: The peaceful demonstration between Michelle Bolsonaro and Flávio Bolsonaro was viewed positively by 59% of Brazilians, according to a Genial/Quaest poll. The former first lady’s support was well received and boosts the senator’s prospects in the 2026 presidential race.

item.title: O que mantém Lula à frente em pesquisa apesar da percepção de piora da economia
item.description: Despite negative economic perceptions — with 43% of Brazilians saying the economy worsened and 68% seeing higher food prices — Lula maintains a lead over Flávio Bolsonaro in a hypothetical runoff, with 44% versus 39%. The Genial/Quaest poll indicates that strong rejection of the Bolsonaro surname is a key factor behind this advantage, even amid unfavorable views on purchasing power and employment. Another 13% would vote blank/null or for neither candidate, and 4% are undecided.

item.title: Entenda como a analogia do “castelo de cartas” traduz a segurança da urna eletrônica
item.description: The Brazilian electronic voting machine is designed to detect any unauthorized alteration to its physical components or software, immediately halting operation if a change is detected — analogous to a house of cards that collapses if a single card is removed. This verification runs continuously from startup via dedicated security processors like the Embedded Security Module (MSE) and cannot be disabled, ensuring vote integrity even against fraud attempts.

item.title: Novo questiona Lula após pagamentos a ex-assessor
item.description: The Novo Party questioned whether President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will again claim ignorance regarding payments made by lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger to his former chief of staff, Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro (Marcola), between January 2023 and July 2026. The amounts, in the tens of thousands of reais, remain undisclosed and are under Federal Police investigation. Roberta also has close ties to Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha), the president’s son, who is under multiple investigations, including for influence peddling.

item.title: Republicanos oficializa candidatura de Pivetta ao governo de MT
item.description: Governor Otaviano Pivetta was officially nominated as the Republicans' candidate for re-election in Mato Grosso during a convention in Cuiabá. He selected federal deputy Fabio Garcia (União Brasil) as his running mate for vice-governor. His main opponent is Senator Wellington Fagundes (PL), who has the backing of Jair and Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: O que explica a melhora de Flávio Bolsonaro contra Lula na Genial/Quaest
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro narrowing the gap with Lula in a hypothetical runoff, reducing Lula’s lead from 8 points in June to 5 points now (44% to 39%). The improvement is driven by stronger performance among conservative men, where Bolsonaro now leads 44% to 40%, reversing a prior deficit. His support also rose among non-Bolsonarist right-wing voters (from 53% to 66%) and pure Bolsonarists (from 91% to 95%).

item.title: Após reunião com Milei, Tarcísio e Nunes se reúnem com chanceler do Chile em SP
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas and Mayor Ricardo Nunes met in São Paulo with Chile’s Foreign Minister Francisco MacKeena to discuss public security, international cooperation, and shared challenges in combating organized crime. The meeting is part of an effort to strengthen ties with right-wing leaders in the region, aligning views between São Paulo, Buenos Aires, and Santiago on economy and security, following prior engagements with Javier Milei and Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Patrimônio de Zoe Martínez cresce 226% em dois anos
item.description: PL candidate for the Chamber of Deputies in São Paulo, Zoe Martínez, saw her declared assets to the Electoral Justice grow by 226% over two years, rising from R$646,000 to R$2.1 million. The increase represents an addition of approximately R$1.46 million between 2022 and 2024.

item.title: Tarifaço passa a impor perdas também a Lula, mostra Genial/Quaest
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows that although Lula is still seen as better representing Brazil’s interests than Flávio Bolsonaro (46% to 38%), his lead has narrowed from 17 to 8 percentage points due to the impact of the U.S. tariff increase. This reflects a weakening perception of Lula on external economic issues, despite maintaining a relative advantage.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio avalia que manutenção do patamar na Quaest após reveses com Centrão reduz temor de desgaste por isolamento
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro’s stability in the Genial/Quaest poll, with 30% in the first round (up from 28%), was welcomed by his campaign as relief despite changes being within the margin of error. Maintaining his level reduces fears of immediate damage from partisan isolation after failed Centrão alliances. In a potential runoff, Lula leads with 44% versus Flávio’s 39%, also within the two-point margin of error.

item.title: Lula perde terreno para quase todos os desafiantes, indica Quaest
item.description: Lula loses ground against nearly all challengers in Quaest’s second-round simulations. The only candidate who did not reduce his disadvantage was Romeu Zema (Novo). Against the former Minas Gerais governor, Lula maintains 46% of voting intentions.

item.title: Tarcísio de Freitas diz que não colocaria boné de Donald Trump novamente
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas said he would not wear the Make America Great Again hat again after the U.S. imposed tariffs on Brazilian products. He stated that wearing the hat during Trump’s January 2025 inauguration was unrelated to subsequent trade measures and denied that Eduardo Bolsonaro influenced the U.S. decision. To mitigate the tariffs’ impact, the São Paulo government released accumulated ICMS credits to support businesses.

item.title: Quaest: para 52%, decisão de proibir visitas a Jair Bolsonaro está errada
item.description: A Quaest poll shows 52% of respondents believe banning Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting his father, Jair Bolsonaro, is wrong, while 41% support the measure. Opinions sharply divide along political lines: 92% of Bolsonaro supporters oppose the ban, whereas 70-73% of Lula supporters and non-Lula left-wing voters approve it. Among independents, 50% view the ban as incorrect.

item.title: “Deputado Paulo Pimenta, tome vergonha na cara”
item.description: Rio Grande do Sul Governor Eduardo Leite (PSD) released a video refuting claims made by federal deputy Paulo Pimenta (PT-RS), a Senate candidate, telling him to "have some shame". Leite said he was outraged by Pimenta's allegations, though specific accusations were not detailed in the excerpt. The video was posted in response to Pimenta's criticisms, escalating political tensions between the two in the state.

item.title: Lula x Flávio: o que mudou na disputa entre julho e agosto, segundo a pesquisa Quaest
item.description: The August Genial/Quaest poll shows the presidential race between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro has tightened: Lula dropped from 40% to 39% in the first round and from 45% to 44% in the second, while Flávio rose from 28% to 30% and from 37% to 39%, respectively. Despite Flávio's gains, Lula remains ahead in both scenarios, preserving his frontrunner status, and the third-place space saw Renan Santos and Ronaldo Caiado tie at 4% each, indicating a redistribution within the third bloc without altering the race's polarized structure.

item.title: CEO da Quaest: pazes com Michelle e reação ao STF impulsionaram Flávio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's growth in the Genial/Quaest poll was driven by his reconciliation with Michelle Bolsonaro and voter backlash against the STF's decision barring him from visiting jailed Jair Bolsonaro. According to Quaest CEO Felipe Nunes, this reorganized the right and brought anti-PT voters back to consider Flávio, increasing his support among both Bolsonaro loyalists and non-Bolsonaro conservatives.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: 68% não sabiam da reunião de Flávio com embaixadores sobre as eleições
item.description: Genial/Quaest poll shows 68% of Brazilians were unaware of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's meeting with ambassadors, where he repeated false claims about Smartmatic and electronic voting machines, already debunked by the TSE. Among independent voters, 75% said they had no knowledge of the event. While 54% say the incident does not affect their voting intention, 26% say it decreased and 15% say it increased. Among Bolsonaro supporters, 45% said the remarks increased their support for Flávio.

item.title: Lula teme interferência na eleição e amplia crises com EUA e Argentina
item.description: The Lula government is facing diplomatic crises with the U.S. and Argentina, potentially leaving Brazil without active ambassadors in Washington and Buenos Aires until the 2026 elections. There is concern that governments allied with Trump and Milei may not recognize the election results if Flávio Bolsonaro loses, accusing Brazil of undue interference. The situation is described as a personalist clash between Lula and Milei, lacking any basis in public interest.

item.title: Ideia aponta disparada na rejeição a Flávio
item.description: A Meio/Ideia poll released on November 5 shows Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL-RJ) rejection rose nearly five percentage points since July 6, reaching 48%. Rejection for all five leading presidential candidates increased, as expected, as voters become more familiar with them.

item.title: Faria Lima se volta para noticiário doméstico à espera da Selic
item.description: Financial markets await the Copom's decision on the Selic rate, with expectations of a cut to 14% from 14.25%, while the PL is set to announce its vice-presidential candidate on Flávio Bolsonaro's ticket, reflecting right-leaning support despite dissatisfaction with Lula's main rival. The day includes corporate earnings like Bradesco's, U.S. ADP jobs data, eurozone PPI, and volatile trading after SpaceX shares dropped 11% due to AI investment concerns post-IPO.

item.title: A queda de Lula em setor estratégico do eleitorado em nova pesquisa
item.description: President Lula's voting intention dropped seven points among independent voters in a hypothetical runoff against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, falling from 40% to 33%, while Bolsonaro rose from 27% to 30%, cutting Lula's lead from 13 to just three points — within the margin of error. Lula's approval rating also declined in this group, with disapproval rising to 47% and approval falling to 42%, reversing a July tie. The Genial/Quaest poll surveyed 2,004 people between July 31 and August 3.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: 43% dizem que Lula reagiu mal ao tarifaço; índice avança sete pontos
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows 43% of Brazilians believe President Lula reacted poorly to the new U.S. tariffs, up seven points from May. Meanwhile, 38% approve of his response, 4% see it as neutral, and 15% were undecided. Perception of who best defends Brazil’s interests shifted: Lula dropped from 51% to 46%, while Flávio Bolsonaro rose from 34% to 38%.

item.title: Lula cai 7 pontos entre os independentes no 2º turno contra Flávio, indica Quaest
item.description: Lula (PT) lost 7 percentage points among independent voters in a potential runoff against Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), according to a Genial/Quaest poll released on August 5. His support in this group dropped from 40% in July to 33% in August. The performance of Jair Bolsonaro's son was not detailed in the provided excerpt.

item.title: Pesquisa mostra que a direita começa a se reorganizar e entregas do governo perdem força
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows the Brazilian right is beginning to reorganize, narrowing the gap between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro by three percentage points. Government deliveries under Lula have lost some of their electoral impact, while both Bolsonarist and non-Bolsonarist right-wing voters positively view the relationship between Flávio and Michelle Bolsonaro (88% and 90%, respectively).

item.title: Vantagem de Flávio sobre Lula entre evangélicos cai pela metade, mas senador reduz distância entre independentes
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's lead over Lula among evangelicals dropped from 15 to 7 percentage points, according to Genial/Quaest poll. However, the senator narrowed the gap with Lula among independent voters by 10 points. Lula still leads in a potential runoff with 44% to Flávio's 39%, though both saw slight declines since July.

item.title: Um em cada dez eleitores acredita que Lula foi substituído por um clone
item.description: A Meio/Ideia poll shows that 12.5% of Brazilian voters believe President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was replaced by a clone or double, while 58.9% reject the claim as false and 28.5% did not know or did not respond. The conspiracy theory, circulating in obscure online forums since 2022, was humorously referenced by Lula in a Sorocaba speech where he joked about being the 'fifth Lula'.

item.title: Quaest: Flavio oscila pra cima; vantagem numérica de Lula cai nos 2 turnos
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro increased in voting intentions in both first and second round scenarios, within the margin of error, while President Lula decreased but still holds a lead.
